safety.title: If you feel very sad or unsafe
safety.text: These lessons help with study and everyday stress. They are not a doctor. Do you feel very sad or unsafe? Do you think about hurting yourself? Please talk to a parent, teacher or school counsellor today. You matter. Help is there.

topics.title: How to study
topics.summary: Reading again and again teaches little. Testing yourself teaches a lot.

blocks.title: The big idea
blocks.text: Your brain learns when it pulls out an answer. Reading the answer again does not do this. Good study feels a bit hard.

items.x: Not "study biology". Say "learn the parts of the cell".
Read the notes one time. Underline only key words.
Write or say all you remember. This step matters most.
Open the book. Mark what you missed.
Do 5 to 10 questions on the same unit.
Look again tomorrow, then in 3 days, then in a week.

items.q: You have one hour before a test. What helps most?
options: Read once, then test yourself with the book closed
items.why: Testing yourself works better than reading again. It feels harder, but you remember more.

items.q: You study maths. Which plan is better?
items.why: Mixing teaches you to pick the right method. The exam asks you to do that.

items.q: When is the best time to go over a topic again?
options: Only the night before the exam
A little, many times, over some weeks
items.why: Short looks, a few days apart, make memories last longer.

blocks.title: Study timer
blocks.text: Study for 25 minutes. Rest for 5. Do it again.

items: Study one topic for 25 minutes. Close the book for the last 10.
Write 3 questions about today's lesson. Answer them tomorrow.
Tell someone at home one thing you learned.

topics.title: Remember what you read
topics.summary: Four ways to keep what you read in your head.

items.x: One page or one heading.
Close the book or cover the page.
What were the main points? Use your own words.
Look again. What you forgot is what to study.
Learn it. Test yourself.
Test again for 5 minutes.
Test again. It gets easier.
Short looks keep it until the matric.

blocks.title: Review planner
blocks.text: Type what you studied today. 4 tells you when to look again.

items.x: For example, how plants make food.

items.t: Explain it to a young child
items.x: Use easy words and an example from home.
Go back to the book for that part.
Explain again until it is short and clear.
Write the unit name in a circle.
One branch for each part. Use one or two words.
Pictures help you remember.
Try it without looking.

blocks.title: After a chapter, can you…
items: Say the main idea in one sentence?
Give one example?
Answer one past exam question on it?
Draw a small picture of it from memory?
Explain it to a friend?
After each page today, close the book. Say the main point.
Draw one mind map of a unit.
Add today's topic to the review planner.

topics.title: Tricks for solving problems
topics.summary: For maths, physics and chemistry. A simple plan for any problem.

items.x: Read it twice. Write what you know and what you need.
Which rule links them? Have you seen one like it?
Go step by step. Write the units.
Does the answer make sense? A bike cannot go 3000 m/s.
Try simple numbers first. Then use the real ones.
Start from the answer you need. What do you need to find it?
Try 1, 2, 3. What repeats?
Do another question. Come back in 10 minutes.

items.q: You are not sure in a multiple-choice maths question. What first?
options: Put each answer back into the question
items.why: Testing each answer often shows the right one fast.

items.q: Your physics answer has no units. What does it mean?
options: You may have a mistake. Check each step.
items.why: Units are a free check. Wrong units mean a wrong step.

blocks.title: Before you finish a problem
items: I wrote what I know and what I need.
I drew a picture if it helps.
I wrote the formula first.
I wrote the units.
I checked that the answer makes sense.
Solve 3 problems with the four steps.
Find one old mistake. Write why it happened.
Explain one problem to a classmate.

topics.title: How to get ready for exams
topics.summary: A clear plan for tests and the matric. Past papers are the key.

blocks.title: About the matric
blocks.text: The matric is mostly multiple choice. It covers Grade 9 to 12. Old exam papers show you the style. 4 has many, with answers.

items.x: List every unit. Mark each one: strong, okay or weak.
Study weak units first. Do one old paper per subject.
Do more old papers. Study every question you got wrong.
Do full papers with a timer. No phone.
Light review and sleep. No big new topics.
Pack pens, pencil, eraser and ID. Sleep at your usual time.
How many questions? How much time? How to fill the answer sheet?
Do not spend 10 minutes on one question.
Answer what you know. Mark hard ones. Come back later.
Picking from two is easier than from four.
Question 23 on the paper is 23 on the sheet.

blocks.title: Exam week list
items: I know the date, time and place of each exam.
I did at least one full old paper per subject.
I studied my past mistakes.
I have pens, pencils, eraser and ruler.
I will sleep 8 hours each night.
I will eat breakfast and bring water.

blocks.title: Timed practice
blocks.text: Do old exam questions for 25 minutes. Then rest.

items: List your units. Mark each strong, okay or weak.
Do 20 questions from one old matric paper in 4.
Write down each mistake and the right answer.

topics.title: Fear before exams
topics.summary: Feeling nervous is normal. A little helps you focus. Here is how to stay calm.

blocks.title: How worried am I before exams?
blocks.intro: Be honest. Only you see this.
questions: I can't sleep the night before an exam.
My heart beats fast or my stomach hurts.
My mind goes blank, even when I studied.
I keep thinking I will fail.
I don't study because the exam scares me.
I worry what my family will say.
After an exam, I keep thinking about my mistakes.
I shake or sweat in the exam room.

bands.title: Mostly calm
bands.advice: You handle exam nerves well. Use calm breathing on hard days.

bands.title: Some nerves
bands.advice: This is very common. Do old papers with a timer. Breathe slowly before you start.

bands.title: Quite worried
bands.advice: Worry is getting in your way. Use the steps below each day. Talk to someone you trust.

bands.title: Very worried
bands.advice: This is a lot to carry alone. Please talk to a parent, teacher or school counsellor soon.

blocks.title: Why your body reacts
blocks.text: Before an exam, your heart beats fast. This is your body getting ready. It does not mean you will fail. Slow breathing calms your body.

blocks.title: Calm breathing (4-7-8)
blocks.text: Breathe in for 4. Hold for 7. Breathe out for 8. Do it 4 times.

items.x: Old papers with a timer make the real exam feel normal.
Before the exam, write them on paper. Your mind feels lighter.
Call the feeling energy, not fear.
One quick win calms you.
Put the pen down. Take 3 slow breaths. Go to the next question.

items: Do calm breathing now, and again before bed.
Do one old paper with a timer.
Tell one person how you feel about exams.

topics.title: Better memory
topics.summary: Memory can grow. Sleep and simple tricks make it stronger.

items.x: Teenagers need this. Sleep saves what you learned today.
Walk, run or play football. It helps your brain and mood.
A hungry brain can't focus.
Breaks help new things stick.
Make a word from first letters. Colours of light: ROY G BIV.
Put a list into a simple tune.
Remember 0917 2346 as two groups, not eight numbers.
Strange pictures stick. See the cell's mitochondria as a power station.
Your home, or your walk to school.
Gate, door, kitchen, window, bed.

items.t: Put one thing at each stop
items.x: Planets: Mercury at the gate, Venus at the door…
See each thing at its stop. Do it twice.

items.q: You studied until 2 am. You slept 4 hours. What happens?
options: You lose a lot. Sleep helps save memories.
items.why: Sleep moves new learning into long memory. Short sleep means you forget more.

items.q: Which list is easiest to remember?
options: Words placed on a path you know
items.why: A memory walk links new things to places you know well.

items: Make a memory walk with 5 stops for one list.
Go to bed 30 minutes earlier tonight.
Make one first-letter trick for your notes.

topics.title: Putting things off
topics.summary: Putting things off (procrastination) is not laziness. We avoid a bad feeling. Make the start tiny.

blocks.title: Do I put things off?
blocks.intro: Think about the last two weeks.
questions: I start homework on the last day.
I pick up my phone when I sit down to study.
I do other jobs so I don't have to study.
I tell myself "later" or "tomorrow".
I feel bad about wasted time.
Big tasks feel too big to start.

bands.title: Not much
bands.advice: You start most tasks on time. Keep it up.

bands.title: Sometimes
bands.advice: Like most students. Try the 2-minute start and a timer.

bands.title: A lot
bands.advice: It is a habit now. Habits can change. Use the steps below for a week.

blocks.title: Why we wait
blocks.text: We wait when a task feels boring, hard or scary. Waiting feels good now. Later it brings stress. So make the start very small.

blocks.title: 2-minute start
blocks.text: Do the task for only 2 minutes. Then you may stop. Most times, you will go on.

items.x: "Study chemistry" becomes "write the first 10 elements".
"At 4 pm, I open my maths book at the table."
Put it in another room before you start.
After studying, have tea, see friends or play.

items: Pick the task you avoid most. Do it for 2 minutes.
Write a time and place for tomorrow's study.
Put your phone in another room while you study.

topics.title: Feeling lazy or not wanting to study
topics.summary: Wanting to study often comes after you start. Small wins help. So does a reason you care about.

blocks.title: How is my drive to study?
blocks.intro: Think about the last two weeks.
questions: I feel tired, even after enough sleep.
I don't see why school matters for me.
I start tasks but stop quickly.
I think I will fail, so why try.
I don't enjoy things I used to enjoy.

bands.title: Doing okay
bands.advice: Your drive is steady. Set a goal to aim higher.

bands.title: A bit low
bands.advice: This is common. Find your reason. Get small wins each day.

bands.title: Very low
bands.advice: This may be more than laziness. Feeling low for two weeks? Talk to a parent, teacher or counsellor.

items.x: Why study? A job you want? Helping your family? Write it down.
One question. One page. Doing it brings the wish to do more.
Mark each day you study. Try not to break the chain.
A friend who studies too keeps you going.
Low energy can come from short sleep or no breakfast.

blocks.title: My reason and my goal
blocks.text: Write why you study. Write one small goal for this week.

items: Write your reason on paper. Put it where you study.
Do one 10-minute task right now.
Ask a friend to study with you tomorrow.

topics.title: Unkind thoughts about yourself
topics.summary: "I am stupid." "I will never pass." Thoughts are not facts. You can change them.

blocks.title: How kind is my inner voice?
blocks.intro: How often do you think this?
questions: "I am stupid."
"Everyone is better than me."
"I always fail."
"One mistake means I am a failure."
"There is no point trying."
"I will let everyone down."

bands.title: Mostly kind
bands.advice: You are fair to yourself. Keep it up.

bands.title: Sometimes harsh
bands.advice: Many students are hard on themselves. Try the worksheet below.

bands.title: Very harsh
bands.advice: These thoughts hurt. Use the worksheet each day. Tell someone you trust how you feel.

blocks.title: Catch it, check it, change it

items.x: Notice the thought. Say: "I am having the thought that I am stupid."
Is it 100% true? What shows it is not true?
Make it fair: "This is hard. I can learn it with practice."
What would you tell your best friend? Tell yourself the same.

blocks.title: Change the thought
blocks.text: Write the bad thought. Check it. Write a fairer one.

blocks.title: Add the word "yet"
blocks.text: Change "I can't do this" to "I can't do this yet." Skills grow with practice.

items: Write one unkind thought. Change it into a fair one.
Add "yet" to one "I can't" sentence.
Write 3 things you did well this week.

topics.title: Comparing yourself with others
topics.summary: Comparing yourself with others steals your joy. Good competition pushes you. Bad competition hurts you.

blocks.title: Do I compare too much?
questions: I feel bad when a friend gets a higher mark.
I hide my marks from others.
I watch other people's marks more than mine.
I don't share notes, so others don't do better.
I feel good only if I am the best.

bands.title: Healthy
bands.advice: You keep your eyes on your own road. Good.

bands.title: Sometimes
bands.advice: Normal, but watch it. Compare with your old self.

bands.title: Too much
bands.advice: Comparing is hurting you. Try the steps below.

items.x: Look at your marks last month and now. That is fair.

items.t: Everyone starts in a different place
items.x: Some have a quiet room or a helper. You can't see their whole story.
Ask a top student how they study. Most will share.
Teaching others helps you learn. Your class is a team.

items.t: Social media shows only good days
items.x: People post their best moments. They have bad days too.

items: Write your last two test marks. See your own progress.
Ask a classmate how they study one subject.
Help someone with a question you understand.

topics.title: Believing in yourself
topics.summary: Confidence is not something you wait for. It grows from small brave steps.

blocks.title: How do I see myself?
questions: I have good things about me.
I can do things as well as most people.
I am a person who matters.
I can speak in class when I want.
A bad mark does not make me worthless.

bands.title: Low right now
bands.advice: You are very hard on yourself. Try the steps below. Talk to someone you trust.

bands.title: In the middle
bands.advice: Like many teenagers. Get small wins. Notice what you are good at.

bands.title: Strong
bands.advice: You see your value. Use it to help others too.

items.t: List what you are good at
items.x: Not only marks. Kind? Hard-working? Good at football?
Ask one question in class this week.
Each day, write one thing that went well.
Sleep, food and exercise help you feel ready.
Pick friends who lift you up.

blocks.title: This week I will…
items: Ask or answer one question in class.
Write 3 things I am good at.
Thank myself for one thing I did well.
Try something new for 10 minutes.
Write 3 things you are good at. Keep the paper in your notebook.
Write one win in a notebook tonight.
Speak once in class tomorrow.

topics.title: Using your time well
topics.summary: School, home jobs and the walk take a lot of time. A simple week plan helps.

items.x: School, the walk, chores, prayer, meals, helping at home.
Look for 30 to 60 free minutes. Early morning is often quiet.
Weak subjects get more time.
Read and write in daylight. Test yourself in the evening.
Rest is part of the plan.
Go over the last lesson in your head.
Look at five flash cards.
Do it while your mind is fresh.

blocks.title: My week
items: I wrote my fixed times.
I found at least 5 study times.
Each subject has a time.
I planned rest.
I will check my plan on Sunday.

blocks.title: Study timer
blocks.text: 25 minutes of study makes time feel short and clear.

items: Draw your week plan on one page.
On the walk to school, go over one lesson.
Do your hardest task first tomorrow.

topics.title: Focus and your phone
topics.summary: Each message pulls you away. Coming back takes minutes. Protect your focus.

blocks.title: Does my phone pull me away?
questions: I check my phone while studying.
My phone is next to me when I study.
I lose time on videos or chats.
I use my phone in bed late.
I feel nervous if I can't check it.

bands.title: In control
bands.advice: You handle your phone well.

bands.title: Some
bands.advice: Try one study time with no phone.

bands.title: A lot
bands.advice: Your phone takes study and sleep time. Use the steps below each day.

items.x: Even a phone face-down pulls you. Put it in another room.
Study and chat together make both slow.
4 works offline. Turn data off while you study.
Messages can wait 25 minutes.
Late chats steal your sleep.

blocks.title: No-phone study time
blocks.text: Start 25 minutes. The phone stays away until the break.

items: Study once with your phone in another room.
Turn data off during homework.
No phone for 30 minutes before sleep.

topics.title: Sleep and health
topics.summary: Sleep, food, water and exercise help you study. A rested brain learns faster.

blocks.title: How are my sleep and health?
blocks.intro: In the last week, how often…
questions: I slept less than 7 hours.
I skipped breakfast.
I drank strong coffee or tea late in the day.
I used a screen in bed.
I felt sleepy in class.
I did no walking, running or sport.

bands.title: Healthy
bands.advice: Good habits. Your brain thanks you.

bands.title: Could be better
bands.advice: Pick one habit below to fix this week.

bands.title: Needs care
bands.advice: Your body is tired. Sleep comes first, even in exam time.

items.x: Sleep and wake at about the same time each day.
Teenagers need this much.
Coffee keeps you awake for hours. Have it in the morning.
Last 30 minutes: no screens. Read, pray or talk calmly.
No sleep makes you forget more.
Even bread and tea is better than nothing.
Keep a bottle with you. Thirst feels like tiredness.
Walk, run or play for 20 minutes most days.

blocks.title: Calm breathing before sleep
blocks.text: A few rounds in bed can help you fall asleep.

items: Go to bed at a set time tonight.
Drink a glass of water now.
Take a 20-minute walk today.

topics.title: Stress and pressure from family
topics.summary: Your family wants the best for you. That can feel heavy. Talking helps.

blocks.title: You are not alone
blocks.text: Many students feel pressure to pass the matric. Some feel pushed to a path. Your family's worry often comes from love and hope.

blocks.title: How much pressure do I feel?
questions: I feel my family cares only about my marks.
I am scared to show my report card.
I have too many home jobs to study.
I must study a subject I don't like.
I feel stressed most days.

bands.title: Okay
bands.advice: You handle the pressure well. Keep talking with your family.

bands.title: Quite a lot
bands.advice: Try a calm talk with your family. See the steps below.

bands.title: Very heavy
bands.advice: This is a lot. Please talk to a teacher, a relative or a school counsellor.

items.x: Not right after a bad mark. Maybe after dinner or coffee.
Families worry less when they see a study plan.
"I want to do well too. Your support helps me."
Agree on hours for chores and hours for study.
A teacher or uncle can help you talk to your parents.

blocks.title: Calm breathing
blocks.text: When stress grows, breathe slowly 4 times.

items: Write 3 sentences you want to tell your family.
Show your study plan to a parent.
Do one thing just for you today.

topics.title: Bad marks and failing
topics.summary: A bad mark does not say who you are. It shows what to learn next.

items.x: It is okay to feel sad or angry for a while.
Where did you lose marks?
Didn't know it? Read it wrong? Ran out of time?
Didn't know: study it. Read wrong: underline key words.
Do similar questions in 4. Watch yourself get better.

items.q: What helps most with a failed test?
options: Study each wrong answer and why
Decide you are bad at it
items.why: Mistakes show you what to learn next. 4 keeps them on the Mistakes page.

items.q: Which thought helps more after a bad mark?
options: "I failed this test. I can find out why."
items.why: One test is not who you are. Fair thoughts help you act.

blocks.title: My mistake check
items: I listed every wrong question.
I wrote the kind of each mistake.
I studied the right answers.
I tried 5 similar questions.
I asked my teacher how to improve.

blocks.title: Many great people failed first
blocks.text: Thomas Edison tried thousands of things before his light bulb worked.

items: List the 3 mistakes you make most.
Try your old mistakes again on the Mistakes page in 4.
Say to yourself what you would tell a friend who failed.

topics.title: Pressure from friends
topics.summary: Friends matter a lot. Good friends support your goals. You can say no and stay friends.

blocks.title: How much do friends push me?
questions: I skip study because friends want to go out.
I do things I don't want, to fit in.
I hide that I like studying.
Friends laugh at my goals.
I find it hard to say no.

bands.title: Low
bands.advice: You make your own choices. Good.

bands.title: Some
bands.advice: Practise the ways to say no below.

bands.title: Strong
bands.advice: Friends pull you a lot. Who supports your goals? Feel unsafe? Talk to an adult you trust.

items.x: "No, thanks. I have to study tonight."
"Not now. Let's play football on Saturday."
"My family needs me at home."
You don't need a long reason.
Spend time with friends who also want to pass.

items.q: Friends want to skip class and go to town. You have a test tomorrow.
options: "I can't today. Let's meet after school."
Go, and lie to your family
items.why: Saying no and offering another time keeps your plan and your friends.

items: Say one "No, thanks" sentence out loud.
Plan one study time with a friend who has goals.
Notice one time today you chose what you wanted.

topics.title: Setting goals
topics.summary: A clear goal shows you where to go. Make it small and clear, with a date.

items.x: Not "do better in maths". Say "get 70% in the next maths test".
A mark, a number of papers, or pages.
From 40% to 60% is better than 40% to 100%.
It helps you reach the matric or the job you want.
"By the end of this term."
Pass the matric with good marks.
Finish the Grade 11 units. Do 3 old papers per subject.
Biology unit 3 and one old paper.
30 minutes on cell division. Then 10 questions.

blocks.title: My goal
blocks.text: Write one goal and your first small step.

items: Write one goal for this term.
Cut it into steps for this week.
Do today's step.

topics.title: Studying in a group
topics.summary: Studying together can help a lot. Or it can waste the day. Here is how to make it work.

items.x: 3 or 4 people who want to learn.
"Today: chemistry unit 4 questions."
Come ready. The group is for testing each other.
Each person explains one part. Teaching helps you learn.
Use old exam questions. Explain every answer.
Chat and tea at break time only.

blocks.title: Before the next group meeting
items: We picked a topic.
Everyone studied it alone first.
Each person has 3 questions ready.
We have a time and place.
Phones stay away while we study.
Invite 2 classmates to study one topic for an hour.
Get 3 questions ready for the group.
Explain one idea to the group.

topics.title: Asking for help
topics.summary: Asking for help is a skill, not a weakness. People like to help when you ask clearly.

items.x: Try for 10 minutes. Then show what you did.
Not "I don't get physics". Say "I don't get step 3 here".
After class or at break.
Then try a similar question alone.
They know the lessons and the exam.
A friend can explain in simple words.

items.t: An older brother, sister or cousin
items.x: Many have done the matric before you.
Ask about any topic. It works with no internet.
For stress, worry or problems at home.

blocks.title: Before I ask
items: I tried for at least 10 minutes.
I know which part I don't understand.
I wrote my question down.
I picked a good time to ask.
Write one question. Ask a teacher tomorrow.
Ask the Tutor in 4 about a hard topic.
Help a classmate who asks you.

topics.title: Grade 12 away from home
topics.summary: Living away from home for Grade 12 is a big change. A daily routine helps.

blocks.title: A new start
blocks.text: Many students do Grade 12 and the matric at Sawa. Missing home is normal, most of all in the first weeks.

items.x: Set times for study, rest and sleep.
Study with students from your class or town.
One bag or box for each subject.
A short call or message when you can.
Drink water. Sleep enough. Say if you feel unwell.

blocks.title: My first week
items: I know my class timetable.
I made a study routine.
I found at least one study friend.
My notes are sorted by subject.
I know who to talk to if I feel sick or sad.

blocks.title: When you miss home
blocks.text: Slow breathing calms you when you feel homesick.

items: Write tomorrow's routine with study times.
Ask one classmate to study with you this week.
Write a short message to your family.
